subject: Prod latency spike - EU pathing issue (escalation)
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightbeam.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T08:12:00Z
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 latency spikes — impacting production

Hi Neha,

We're seeing a sharp jump in p95 and p99 RTTs for requests originating from EU users starting last night (2028-06-14 23:30 UTC). Error rate is up ~2.5% and tail latency is affecting customer journeys — retries are cascading. Attached are a couple of sample request traces and request IDs (brightbeam_sample_traces.txt).

Key notes:
- Region: eu-west-1
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings (hosted API)
- Sample request IDs: rb-ff7a, rb-ff7b, rb-ff9c

Can you confirm whether this is a known change on your side or if we should open an incident? We have customers escalating to our ops team.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Patel
Platform Lead, BrightBeam Health
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightbeam.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T08:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spikes — impacting production

Sam — thanks for the heads up and the traces, we're on it. I've looped in Marissa (CS) and Jonas (infra) to investigate immediately.

Next steps:
- Jonas to collect routing/eBPF traces and check cross-region egress mappings.
- Marissa will coordinate a short incident call if we confirm customer impact beyond normal variance.
- I'll provide a remediation ETA within 60 minutes.

In the meantime, could you confirm whether your requests include any explicit region pins or headers? Also confirm the scale (rps) you're seeing from EU clients.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T08:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Sudden p95/p99 latency spikes — impacting production

Forwarding customer traces and initial context. Sam reports EU p95/p99 jump starting ~23:30 UTC. I already checked customer config — no region pinning on their side. Attaching the trace snapshot I pulled from their payloads (initial-trace-snapshot.zip).

Observations from our dashboards (quick):
- EU egress p95 jumped from ~110ms to ~420ms at ~23:28 UTC
- Error rate up slightly on /v1/generate only
- Host-level CPU/GPU don't show saturation spikes

Jonas/hannah: can you prioritize routing/eBPF and any inter-region routing logs? If this is an egress mapping issue (EU -> US hairpin), we'll need an emergency routing change and customer credit offer.

Thanks — Marissa
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p95/p99 latency spikes — impacting production

Quick update from infra triage: we've confirmed an increase in median inter-region hop counts for a subset of EU egress traffic. Preliminary cause appears to be a recent change in our edge routing policy that introduced an erroneous egress policy for the eu-west cluster: a CIDR rule in the new policy accidentally matched EU traffic and forwarded it to the us-east routing pool (policy rollout 2028-06-14 22:50 UTC).

I attached the diff that shows the unintended prefix match (egress-policy-diff.patch). Steps I'm taking now:
- Roll back the last routing policy (immediate)
- Force a re-sync of egress maps to EU edge nodes
- Monitor p95/p99 and traceroutes for the next 10 minutes

If rollback is insufficient, we'll apply an emergency route override to pin EU egress to the eu-west pool. ETA for rollback: 10 minutes.

Jonas
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightbeam.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spikes — impacting production

Sam — quick status update: Jonas identified a routing policy rollout that produced an accidental prefix match sending some EU traffic to our US egress pool. Jonas is rolling back the policy now and forcing egress map re-syncs. ETA from infra is ~10 minutes to verify improvement.

What we're doing for you:
- Immediate rollback + egress re-sync (in progress)
- If needed, emergency route override to pin EU egress
- Post-incident credits for impacted windows and a follow-up postmortem
- Executive call offered with Markus Klein (VP) if you'd like to discuss impact/credits — available today at 16:00 UTC.

I'll update again as soon as Jonas confirms p95 is returning to baseline. Thanks for your patience.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-17T15:09:00Z
Subject: Postmortem: EU egress routing misconfiguration (INC-4821)

Summary:
- Incident window: 2028-06-14 22:50 UTC -> 2028-06-15 09:00 UTC
- Root cause: Rollout of new egress routing policy that contained an overbroad prefix rule; EU traffic matched and was egressed via US pool, increasing RTT and p95/p99.
- Impact: BrightBeam Health and other EU customers saw p95 increase from ~110ms to ~420ms, small increase in 5xx errors for /v1/generate.

Actions taken:
1) Rolled back faulty routing policy (Jonas) and forced egress map re-syncs to edge nodes.
2) Applied temporary emergency override to pin EU egress until policy rollout is hardened.
3) Created follow-up Jira: INC-4821 to track permanent fix and test coverage for prefix rules.
4) Customer remediation: Offered credit for impacted window and an executive call (Markus).

Attachments: routing-config-diff.txt, egress-policy-diff.patch, initial-trace-snapshot.zip

Follow-ups (owners):
- Rafael: add unit and integration tests to policy compiler to prevent overbroad matches (due 2028-06-24).
- Jonas: add canary verification step for egress policy rollouts and a preflight CIDR scanner (due 2028-06-21).
- Marissa/Neha: finalize customer credit and close INC-4821 (due 2028-06-18).

Links: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INC-4821, https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/runbooks/egress-failover-runbook.pdf

Let me know if any other details are needed for BrightBeam's audit.

-Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
